title: Group Work on a Business Plan

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Let's review your group's business plan. Josh, remind me what the business is.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: It's a mobile coffee cart that serves students on campus. We'd start with one cart outside the library.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We surveyed a hundred and twenty students. Seventy per cent said they buy coffee at least three times a week, and sixty per cent said they'd prefer a cheaper option than the campus café.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Those are encouraging figures, but how did you choose your sample? If you only asked students who were queuing for coffee, the results might be biased.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We approached people at random in the library and the student union, so I think it's fairly representative.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: A second-hand cart costs about two thousand pounds, and we estimate monthly costs at six hundred pounds for ingredients and permits. If we sell two hundred cups a day at two pounds each, we'd earn about eight thousand pounds a month.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: That's the revenue, not profit. Have you included your own wages? And have you considered that sales fall in the holidays?

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We hadn't factored in the holidays. Term time is about thirty weeks a year.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Then your annual revenue is considerably lower than your monthly figure suggests. Please recalculate with realistic assumptions.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We'll do a best case, a worst case and a middle scenario.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Excellent approach. Now, what about competition from the campus café?

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We think the café's prices are too high, and our cart offers convenience, because it's closer to the lecture halls.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Convenience is a real advantage, but don't assume the café won't respond. They could lower prices or start a loyalty scheme. Your plan should explain what makes you hard to copy.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Our idea is to use only locally roasted beans and reusable cups, with a discount for students who bring their own.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: That's a distinctive selling point, and it fits with growing concern for the environment. However, check that reusable cups comply with hygiene regulations.

transcript.speaker: S3
transcript.text: We've already contacted the council about the permit. They said it takes about three weeks, and the fee is eighty pounds a year. We also plan to open a social media page, so students can see the daily menu and special offers before they leave their lectures.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good. One last point: the presentation is on the ninth of May. Each of you should speak for about five minutes, and I'd like a one-page summary of the financial forecast.
